name: Combined T and B Cell Immunodeficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ESID Diagnostic Criteria for Severe Combined Immunodeficiency

criteria.description: Profound lymphopenia with markedly reduced T and B lymphocytes in peripheral blood
Severe hypogammaglobulinemia with absent or severely reduced immunoglobulin levels
Identification of pathogenic mutation in genes associated with combined immunodeficiency (e.g., IL2RG, RAG1/2, ADA)
Recurrent, severe, or opportunistic infections including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia or chronic viral infections

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of profound T and B lymphopenia with hypogammaglobulinemia plus clinical history of severe or opportunistic infections; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Newborn screening by T-cell receptor excision circles (TREC) assay is increasingly used for early detection

pathognomonic.symptomName: Profound lymphopenia affecting T and B cells
searchTerms: very low T and B lymphocyte counts
frequent serious infections from weak immunity

common.symptomName: Chronic diarrhea due to gastrointestinal infections

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby

occasional.symptomName: Chronic skin infections including eczema and abscesses
searchTerms: chronic skin infections like eczema and abscesses

occasional.symptomName: Failure to respond to standard vaccinations
searchTerms: failure to develop immunity after vaccination

rare.symptomName: Autoimmune manifestations such as hemolytic anemia
Chronic lung disease due to repeated infections
searchTerms: long-term lung damage from repeated infections
chronic lung disease due to infections

laboratory: Severe lymphopenia with markedly reduced CD3+ T cells and CD19+ B cells
Hypogammaglobulinemia with low or absent IgG, IgA, and IgM
Absent or severely reduced T-cell receptor excision circles (TREC) on newborn screening
imaging: Chest X-ray showing pneumonia or interstitial infiltrates
CT scan may reveal bronchiectasis in chronic cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as IL2RG, RAG1, RAG2, ADA, JAK3, or others causing combined immunodeficiency
other: Failure to thrive and poor weight gain
Positive family history of early infant deaths or immunodeficiency

distinguishingFeatures: Absent B cells but normal or near-normal T cell numbers
ADA enzyme deficiency confirmed by biochemical assay

redFlags: Severe, recurrent, or opportunistic infections in early infancy
Failure to thrive despite adequate nutrition
Profound lymphopenia on complete blood count
